assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action) has been converted into therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with large outcome trials showing cardiovascular and renal benefit. Rare combination of clear physiology, rigorous mechanism and enormous clinical and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its secretion and actions) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology and therapeutic translation) are the most defensible scientific core; Mojsov's contribution (identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form and peptide work) is real but credit is contested. Knudsen, an industrial drug developer (liraglutide, semaglutide), is a plausible alternative, so allocation is a genuine difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent confirmations, approved drugs used by millions, and long-term outcome data. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener-era peptide work and industrial developers is disputed; I rely on my recollection of this history and have not verified it.
Choice of three from four credited names leaves out one person with a strong claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and opening a platform now extending to myeloma and autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulatory CAR design) and June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T) are central; Rosenberg contributed foundational adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cell trials. Other contributors (Eshhar, Brenner and others) are not in the credited names, which complicates fairness of any trio.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated by several approved products and independent trials; long-term durability and safety (toxicities, secondary malignancy) still being characterized, but the core discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Absence of other early CAR pioneers from the credited names limits a fully fair configuration.
Long-term outcomes and applicability to solid tumors remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling: IRE1-mediated splicing of HAC1/XBP1 and downstream stress responses. It is a fundamental principle of cell physiology with deep links to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease. Clear, original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the natural pair, with their respective labs identifying the pathway components and the signal transduction mechanism. Allocation looks clean from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation across yeast and mammals; therapeutic exploitation is still emerging, but the discovery stands on its basic science.
uncertainties: Whether other contributors (for example Sidrauski, Ron, Kaufman, Shen) deserve credit is not captured in the supplied names.
Direct medical impact is more indirect than for therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Importance, originality and clinical consequence are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery and target concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The chemist Zimmermann and the earlier discoverers of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Konopka) are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with more than twenty years of follow-up and strongly replicated outcomes. If anything, recognition is late.
uncertainties: The prize-fair trio omits chemistry and the earlier oncogene discoveries, which may be seen as part of a compound story.
Prior awards for oncogene and cancer genes may reduce novelty of the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal control of defined cell populations with millisecond precision and has reshaped circuit analysis; clinical applications (for example vision restoration) are beginning. Technological impact on basic biology is very large.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth, and Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation) make the credit a compound, crowded story with six names and at most three slots. I choose Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, but this leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck with credible claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with broad independent adoption; therapeutic maturity is still limited.
uncertainties: Attribution is the central difficulty and the choice of three is contestable.
Medical, as opposed to technological, impact is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides for SMN2 (nusinersen) are a landmark of mechanism-based RNA therapy, converting a lethal infantile neuromuscular disease into a treatable one, and validating antisense splicing correction as a platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) are a plausible and compact pair. Others in the SMN2 and ASO field (for example Singh, Hua, Gene Tools-related work) could be argued but are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Clinically established with several years of approved use and independent trials; long-term data and competing modalities (gene therapy, small molecules) are still evolving.
uncertainties: Relative credit of academic and industrial scientists, and of earlier ASO chemistry pioneers, may be contested.
I am familiar with RNA splicing as a field and have tried to apply the common criteria rather than topic preference.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing that single Lgr5+ adult stem cells self-organize into long-lived epithelial organoids created a widely used model of tissue renewal and disease, with applications in cancer, infection and personalized medicine. Originality and breadth of use are strong.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual driver (Lgr5 stem cells, Wnt-dependent culture), with Sato as first author of the foundational organoid work. Two names make a clean configuration, though other organoid pioneers (for example Sasai's pluripotent-derived organoids) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and adopted, but clinical impact is still maturing, so recognition is somewhat early relative to therapeutic candidates.
uncertainties: Whether a Nobel would be given for adult-stem-cell organoids versus the wider organoid field is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data now show strong declines in cervical disease. This is a major cancer-prevention achievement. Zur Hausen's HPV-cancer link was recognized in 2008, but the vaccine itself is a distinct invention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (parallel VLP work and vaccine development) are the supplied credit. The contributions of Zhou, Kirnbauer and others and of intense patent disputes complicate fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with registry evidence of reduced cervical disease and clinical trial confirmation; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP developers (including Zhou) is disputed and I have not verified details.
The topic is partly adjacent to the earlier HPV prize.
